chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Drummer Kid Lips Hackett and the minstrel-show bands
summary: Kid Lips Hackett's stick tricks, later copied by Lionel Hampton and Sonny Payne, and Louis Jordan's start in the Rabbit Foot band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But anyway, getting back to Silas Green, that's where I first heard Bessie Smith. And on the same show, they had a drummer named Kid "Lips" Hackett. And he was an act. He didn't play with the band. But he was an act on stage, and he stood up and played the drums. And he could do all kind

of things with the drumsticks; all kind of things. In fact, later, a few years ago, I was up in Canada with Sweets Edison, and Sonny Payne was with us, and he was doing his tricks with the drumsticks, you know. And he said to me, "I bet you don't know where I got that from." I said, "I'll betcha I do!" [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And he said, "Lionel Hampton?" -- because Hampton was famous for doing it. But they all got it from Kid Lips, you know. I said, "No, you got that from Kid Lips Hackett." That blew his mind, that I even knew about Kid Lips, you know. [LAUGHS] But the man was spectacular. He was a whole show playing the drums. He stood up and played them, you know. But he could throw those drumsticks all kind of places, they'd come back to him, and he'd do all kind of things with the drumsticks, you know. Great personality, Kid Lips Hackett.

And that band used to parade also. But they were more classy than Rabbit Foot. In fact, Louis Jordan came out of that band with Old Man Joe White on the Rabbit Foot Minstrel Show. That's right. They brought Louis Jordan out of Brinkley, Arkansas. That was his first outing, was with the Rabbit Foot Minstrel Show Band. They were stationed down at Fort Gibson, but they'd come to Jackson and play. Their home base was in Fort Gibson, Mississippi. And Silas Green's home base was in Brumley(?), Georgia.
